results.title: How to Overwinter Pepper Plants and Keep Them Alive Until Spring
results.description:
Want to overwinter pepper plants and keep them alive until spring? The right approach depends on whether you want the plant to simply survive winter or continue growing indoors.

Read the full Garden Insider guide:
https://gardeninsider.org/plants/vegetables/how-to-overwinter-pepper-plants/

In this video, you’ll learn how to prepare pepper plants for winter and avoid the most common indoor-care mistakes.

You’ll learn:

- When to bring pepper plants indoors before frost
- How to choose between low-growth winter survival and active indoor growth
- How to inspect peppers for aphids, mites, and hidden pests
- Why isolation matters before placing peppers near houseplants
- When pruning helps and when it can create more stress
- Why healthy roots should not be trimmed automatically
- How winter light changes watering needs
- When to pause fertilizer
- How to judge watering by pot moisture and weight
- Why some leaf drop after moving indoors can be normal
- How to restart growth in spring
- How to harden pepper plants off before returning them outdoors

A pepper plant kept cool with limited growth needs very different care from one growing actively under strong indoor light. The goal should determine how much light, water, pruning, and feeding the plant receives.

How To Overwinter Pepper Plants! (Keep Them Alive For Years) 🥶🌶️
results.description:
Don't let a harsh Canadian winter kill your favourite backyard pepper plants! ❄️🥶🌶️ 

Did you know that peppers like Ghost Peppers and Habaneros are actually perennials that can live for years? Instead of letting them freeze, you can bring them indoors to hibernate! 

In today's video, I am sharing my complete step-by-step beginner's guide on how to safely overwinter pepper plants.
We are breaking down the exact maintenance routine to keep your plants alive until next spring, including:

1. The Aggressive Pruning Step: Why you must chop off all the leaves and trim the branches down to a "Y" shape to conserve energy and eliminate leaf-dwelling pests.
2. The Bare-Root Cleaning Routine: How to safely dig up your plants (whether they are in 5-gallon buckets or fixed raised beds), shake off old garden soil, and give the roots an organic neem oil solution bath to guarantee zero bugs sneak into your house! 🧴🪱
3. Potting Up for Hibernation: Transplanting your clean pepper stems into smaller indoor pots with fresh, moist potting mix.

If you want a massive head start on your pepper harvest next spring, hit that SUBSCRIBE button to join our growing family! ➡️ https://youtube.com/@SeunMoments

🌱 THE OVERWINTERING CHECKLIST:
• The Cut: Strip all leaves and prune branches right above the top nodes.
• The Root Dip: Wash away garden dirt and rinse roots in a neem oil pest bath.
• The Soil: Use fresh, sterile indoor potting mix in a smaller container.
• The Spot: Place in a cool room with indirect window sunlight.

results.title: Overwintering Peppers PNW
results.description:
Hi friends!! 

This fall has been unseasonally warm, which is good because I’m a little late at putting the peppers to bed. Either way, the temps have held out and it’s time to strip the peppers cut them down and prepare them for Dormay over the winter. 

In this video, I talk about the basic concept of overwintering peppers, whether it be in an unheated garage or in a minimally heated house. The basics are to take the peppers down to little knobs, keep them in the area that is cold, but not too cold and to minimally water them. ￼ the success rate varies from plant to plant in year to year, but overwintering peppers is the best way to have a larger yield earlier in the season - plus it’s really fun. 

For those who have been successful in overwintering peppers, please share any tips or unique storage places you have had your peppers for the winter. ￼ for newbies, I hope your peppers thrive! ￼

Thank you for watching and as always, happy gardening!
